observations: Single apple on white background is a true positive (98.0% confidence).
Two grape bunches both detected; an additional overlapping pineapple detection at 33.6% is an incorrect extra class label, even though neither grape is missed.
Tightly packed watermelons: 18 TP, 3 FN; touching and partial visibility complicate detection.
Watermelon field: 5 TP, 1 FP, 14 FN; many distant, small or leaf-obscured fruit are missed.
Market watermelons: 14 TP, 30 FP relative to annotations, 6 FN; distant objects and extra boxes on large foreground fruit are visible.
Orange refrigerator: 10 TP, 39 FP relative to annotations. Many visible oranges are unannotated; these scores conflate incomplete labeling with model errors. No labels were changed.

Confirmed orange-to-kiwi error: images-65-_jpeg.rf.e6b0255b61b10ea30d5dbfff868afb87.jpg has visibly orange fruit; one labeled orange predicted kiwi at 80.6%, IoU 0.912. Other incorrect kiwi/watermelon boxes are present.

Low-confidence example: -_jpg.rf.a3dd29c7ab28e1976f6d339995fd2438.jpg has an unmatched grape box with an overlapping grape prediction at 9.83%, below the fixed 25% threshold. No threshold was changed.
Greedy unmatched-pair analysis found three orange-to-kiwi pairs. This excludes wrong-class extra predictions on already correctly detected objects.
Native Ultralytics confusion matrix uses confidence floor 0.001 and IoU 0.45 for this run; its low-score confusions should not be read as deployment-threshold error counts.
No obvious sustained overfitting: train and validation losses decline; AP50 largely plateaus, AP50-95 makes smaller late gains.
